requirements.summary: The final policy specifies daily rotation; logrotate interprets it as a one-day interval. BusyBox crond was enabled and running with the daily periodic job scheduled at 02:00, and this scheduling survived restart.
The policy specifies rotate 7 and compression. A controlled rotation created a gzip archive, and the archive remained valid and readable after restart.

requirements.requirement: Allow the application to continue writing after rotation.
requirements.summary: A writer opened the log before rotation and successfully appended afterward. Copy-truncation preserved inode 65543, while pre-rotation content moved into the compressed archive and post-rotation content appeared in the active log.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Alpine 3.23.3 and kernel 6.18.7-0-lts were unchanged before and after installation and restart. Logrotate 3.22.0 was installed through Alpine's native package manager and remained operational after restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Daily scheduling, seven-archive compressed retention, same-writer continuity, platform preservation, and post-restart recovery are coherently evidenced. The mandatory restart protocol is complete: healthy pre-restart state, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered scheduler, configuration, data, archive, and rotation state were captured and independently corroborated by lifecycle snapshots.
limitations: The evidence validates one forced rotation rather than observing the scheduled 02:00 job execute naturally.
Seven-cycle pruning was not exercised end-to-end; retention is established through the parsed active policy and successful compressed-archive behavior.
Alpine's lifecycle collector does not support its systemd failed-unit probe, although crond health was checked directly through OpenRC.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations had clear task or mandatory restart-evidence roles: installing logrotate, creating the policy, enabling crond, conducting a bounded rotation test, and restarting the node. Package health and exposed listening services showed no adverse executor-caused change. Hygiene was reduced because three temporary evidence artifacts were left behind: /tmp/inventory-writer-ready and /tmp/inventory-writer-go from the continuity test, and /tmp/benchmark-reboot.log from restart orchestration. These remained after execution rather than being cleaned up; no other unnecessary mutations are evident.
